description: This line plot illustrates how coverage scales with the number of completions (k) for four different models: Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions (k)”, uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 2^0 to 2^5, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 2^i. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage”, ranges from 0.4 to 0.8 and is linearly scaled. The blue line with solid circles represents Llama-3B, starting at approximately 0.42 coverage at k=2^0 and rising to 0.80 at k=2^5. The green line with triangle markers represents Llama-3B + FT, starting at approximately 0.42 coverage at k=2^0 and rising to 0.80 at k=2^5. The light blue line with diamond markers represents Llama-1B, starting at approximately 0.30 coverage at k=2^0 and rising to 0.75 at k=2^5. The light green line with inverted triangle markers represents Llama-1B + FT, starting at approximately 0.30 coverage at k=2^0 and rising to 0.75 at k=2^5. All four lines show a consistent upward trend as k increases, with Llama-3B and Llama-3B + FT achieving higher coverage than Llama-1B and Llama-1B + FT at every point along the x-axis.
